clue.text: Special reporter pretended to be a heroic figure

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, especially a jobbing one
to let on can mean to pretend or make out, as in 'he let on he was ill'

explanation.surface: A special correspondent faked being some kind of hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton led the Endurance expedition to Antarctica, the first of several polar references in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Shackleton, the Antarctic explorer who brought his whole crew home after Endurance sank, is widely regarded as a hero.

clue.text: Spineless sorts of creatures trapping injured wolf

indicators.note: the creatures trap the rearranged letters inside them

parts.note: snakes are creatures, here a definition by example

indicators.note: injured says the letters of wolf are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Cowardly animals have caught a wounded wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spineless' tempts as a zoological word, but snakes have backbones; it means cowardly. 'Injured' rearranges the wolf into OWFL.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowflake is slang for an oversensitive person thought to lack resilience, a spineless type.

clue.text: A great number of years to set up venue

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up turns the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: N stands for an indefinitely large number, as in 'to the nth degree'
an era is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Many years were spent establishing a place for events.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place where sports or shows are staged, a kind of venue.

clue.text: Affinity with a great number below decks?

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, a large number
below decks is in a ship

explanation.surface: A sense of connection among a large crew down in the hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinship is a feeling of close connection or sympathy, a natural affinity.

clue.text: Nun cared about English patient suffering

indicators.note: about means the letters of nun cared are moved around

explanation.surface: A nun tends an English patient who is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like a person in a hospital bed; it is an adjective. Endurance was Shackleton's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to bear hardship patiently over a long time.

clue.text: Good getting into minerals to generate huge figures

indicators.note: the letter for good gets into the word for minerals

parts.note: ores are minerals from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Good things are absorbed into rock to produce giant forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are giants of folklore, huge monstrous figures.

clue.text: Dog circles large seal

indicators.note: the dog goes round the outside of the letter for large, enclosing it

parts.note: a pug is a small snub-nosed breed of dog
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A dog runs round and round a big seal, perhaps at the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a stopper that closes up a hole, just as a seal does.

clue.text: Gentle scatter across top of horizon might be aurora australis

parts.note: a light touch is a gentle one

indicators.note: the word for scatter is spread across the first letter of horizon, holding it inside

parts.note: to sow seed is to scatter it

indicators.note: the top of a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A soft glow spreading over the horizon might be the southern lights.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora australis, or southern lights, is a natural display of coloured light in the polar sky.

clue.text: Drink from boozing.org.uk sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the hidden letters are read in reverse
from says the letters are drawn out of the web address

explanation.surface: A beverage ordered from a booze website is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog is rum diluted with water, the naval drink, and loosely any alcohol.

clue.text: As leaving, draw sailor

indicators.note: the letters of As are leaving, taken away from the word for draw

parts.note: to aspirate is to draw in breath or draw out fluid by suction

explanation.surface: As one departs, one sketches a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching; here it means breathe in or suck out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea, so a seafaring man, a sailor of sorts.

clue.text: Huge expanse of green returning near banks of Amazon

indicators.note: returning means the letters for green come back the other way

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmentally friendly, so green gives ECO

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so take the outside letters of Amazon

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded traveller nears where the Amazon meets the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, the largest expanse on the planet.

clue.text: Brave acts the German drummer displayed across Germany

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: the drummer is spread across the letter for Germany, holding it inside

parts.note: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German drummer performs heroic feats on a tour across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is an old-fashioned word for daring, heroic action.

clue.text: Gordon perhaps stripped here. Exposure doesn't bother him

parts.note: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero, so Flash is one possible first name for a Gordon

indicators.note: stripping a word takes off its outer layer, leaving only its middle letters

explanation.surface: Gordon took his clothes off here, unbothered by being exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposure' looks like weather on bare skin; it is the flasher's habit of exposing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A flasher is a man who exposes himself in public, so exposure is precisely his game.

clue.text: Bit of wood borders northern slope

indicators.note: the strip of wood borders the letter on both sides, holding it inside

parts.note: a slat is a thin narrow strip of wood

explanation.surface: A strip of timber edges a north-facing incline.
explanation.definitionFit: A slant is a sloping or tilted position, the same as an incline.

clue.text: Phrase about 'time' expressed: it's not moving in the slightest

definitions.text: it's not moving in the slightest

indicators.note: the phrase goes about the letter for time, enclosing it

parts.note: a saying is a set phrase or proverb
to put something is to express it, as in 'to put it mildly'

explanation.surface: An expression about time is spoken, describing something perfectly still.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staying put remains where it is and does not shift at all.

clue.text: Make sense of bill presented by Irish politicians

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, so AD
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A bill is tabled by members of an Irish party.
explanation.definitionFit: When an account or story adds up it is coherent and makes sense.

clue.text: Guidelines to store fish in unfinished cabinet

indicators.note: the shortened cabinet stores the fish inside it
unfinished means the last letter of the word for cabinet is lost

parts.note: a dresser is a cabinet or sideboard with shelves
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions for keeping fish in a half-built cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' drops the final letter of the cabinet, leaving DRESSE, and 'store' has it hold the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress code is a set of rules about what to wear, guidelines for attire.

clue.text: Twisted crime has two cardinals hiding in closed shelter

indicators.note: twisted says the letters for crime are bent into another order

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, so crime gives SIN

indicators.note: the two compass points hide inside the word for closed

parts.note: shut means closed
the cardinal points of the compass include east and north, E and N

explanation.surface: A warped criminal has two senior churchmen tucked away in a locked refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' turns SIN into NIS. 'Cardinals' suggests churchmen; here they are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated half-cylinder of corrugated iron used as a military shelter.

clue.text: Places to recover lost Asian artifacts (short on information)

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and come back in a new order
short on means the word for information is missing from artifacts

parts.note: facts are information

explanation.surface: Missing Asian relics, with not much known about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short on information' takes FACTS from ARTIFACTS, leaving ARTI; 'lost' rearranges ASIAN with ARTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanitaria are institutions where invalids convalesce, places to get well.

clue.text: Revenge potentially consuming one from royal family tree

indicators.note: the rearranged letters swallow up the royal letters
potentially says the letters of revenge could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was a member of the British royal family

explanation.surface: Someone's vengeance could swallow up a member of the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges the letters into EVGREEN, which 'consuming' wraps round the royal pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a tree that keeps its leaves all year, such as a pine or holly.

clue.text: Scold fool on opening parts of Antarctic tour

parts.note: a goon is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: the opening parts are the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: An idiot chatters on at the start of an Antarctic expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on at someone is to nag or berate them, the same as scolding.

clue.text: Joker's come back extremely kinky. Awkward!

indicators.note: the joker has come back, so his letters read the other way

parts.note: a wag is a joker; the 's reads as 'has'

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A comedian returns with material far too kinky, causing embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky describes someone clumsy and ungainly, physically or socially awkward.

clue.text: Wilder sibling's creation?

parts.note: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: The work of Gene Wilder's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means an origin or coming into being; it is also the Bible's account of creation.

clue.text: Trekkers courageously holding search in detail

indicators.note: the two words together hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Brave hikers are keeping up a thorough search.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly, leaving no corner unchecked.

clue.text: It goes around or ascends hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending makes the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in southwest England

explanation.surface: Something circles or climbs a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Stress = (2 x 10) ÷ s + n

parts.note: 10 is read two ways, as the word ten and as the letters I and O it resembles; those two are split by S, then N is added

explanation.surface: A mock physics formula for stress, as if from a mechanics textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 x 10' means read 10 twice: as TEN and as the lookalike letters IO. '÷ s' puts S between them, and '+ n' adds N on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental strain or a physical pulling force, both senses of stress.

clue.text: Stacked blocks in gale alternating one ring with another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: alternating picks every other letter of the word gale

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
another ring, another O

explanation.surface: Piled-up blocks in a storm, swapping one ring for another.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter built from stacked blocks of snow.

clue.text: Lose spirit with what Amundsen planted

definitions.meaning: to tire or droop, losing energy
Roald Amundsen planted the Norwegian banner at the South Pole in 1911

explanation.surface: Amundsen's will falters at the moment of triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to weaken or tire, and a flag is the emblem a polar explorer plants on arrival.

clue.text: Attractive person caught behind nurse

indicators.note: the attractive person has caught the word for behind and holds it inside

parts.note: a looker is a good-looking person
aft means at the back, especially on a ship

explanation.surface: A cricket match: a good-looking player is caught behind by the wicketkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught behind' is a cricket dismissal, the ball edged to the wicketkeeper; here 'caught' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to care for them, the same as tending or minding them.

clue.text: Change of heart in those who flock for arduous hike

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for followers is swapped for another

parts.note: sheep move in flocks, and people who blindly follow are called sheep

explanation.surface: Followers of the crowd have a sudden rethink about a gruelling trek.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SHEEP is its middle E; changing it to L gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shlep is a long, tedious journey or trudge, from Yiddish.

clue.text: Glacial erosion carved out geological feature

indicators.note: carving out the inside of each word leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Ice-age erosion has hollowed out a landform.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, typically Scottish, often shaped by glaciers.

clue.text: Outburst gets rat scurrying around bunk

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the word for bunk
the rat scurrying sends the letters of gets rat running into new places

parts.note: a cot is a small bed or berth, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm makes a rat scamper round a bunk bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scurrying' rearranges the letters into GREATST, and 'around' has them wrap the bunk. The exclamation echoes Captain Scott of the Antarctic.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise is a brief outburst, the kind of phrase blurted out in shock.
